facts.fact: UNICEF says NCRA's digital birth and death registration mobile application is used at its registration centres in hospitals, such as the Births and Deaths Office at Ola During Hospital: the child's details are entered there with the application when the mother registers the birth, then transferred to the Central Registry System through the central server, which generates the identification number; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: digital Birth and Death registration mobile application

facts.fact: UNICEF describes births being registered with NCRA's digital birth and death registration mobile application at hospital registration centres, with the certificate ready within 24 hours and more than 200 babies registered a month at Ola During Hospital; the application's name covers deaths but no death registration with it is described; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: digital Birth and Death registration mobile application

facts.fact: UNICEF says the application is the National Civil Registration Authority's, established with UNICEF's support and used at the Authority's own registration centres; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: digital Birth and Death registration mobile application

note: No offices fact: the article names one hospital registration centre and gives no count of centres using the application. The 98 per cent of births notified by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation that were registered in 2022 is a share of births, not of offices. UNICEF's support is not said to be financing, so no finance fact.
